# Australian Public Data MCP

Public-data retrieval and analysis support for any MCP-capable agent.
Australian official sources: ABS, RBA and DCCEEW. Pacific islands: Pacific Data Hub/SPC. Global context: World Bank, OECD, IMF and UN Comtrade.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: installation, MCP client setup, tools and sources
- AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md: analyst guidance supplied during MCP initialization
- AGENTS.md: development rules and architecture
- .mcp.json: project stdio configuration
- ausdata_mcp/server.py: tool contracts and concurrent dispatch
- ausdata_mcp/__main__.py: canonical stdio startup shared by the absolute-path launcher
- ausdata_mcp/artifacts.py: complete evidence storage and bounded manifests/series summaries
- ausdata_mcp/errors.py: structured tool failures with repair guidance and failed request context
- ausdata_mcp/source_http.py: pooled connections, shared per-host GET concurrency, cooldowns and bounded retries
- ausdata_mcp/fetch_cache.py: bounded metadata/file/reference-list caches with concurrent identical-fetch sharing; reference lists expire after one hour and refresh independently
- docs/agent-data-usability.md: research, design decisions and verification limits

Before analysis, confirm the client exposes search_catalog, get_metadata and retrieve directly. Register the stdio server in the client settings if these tools are missing.

Workflow: search_catalog -> select candidate -> get_metadata -> retrieve -> agent reads the complete JSON at artifact_path, filters and analyses it with its own code.
Prefer in-conversation charts and answers. The retrieval JSON is working evidence; do not create extra PNG, CSV, Excel or report files by default unless the user requests an export or the harness needs a temporary display file.
If no suitable dataset is retrievable from a connected source feed, name the feed checked and the specific gap. The publisher may release the data through other channels. Ask before seeking data from websites, downloadable workbooks/CSVs or other APIs unless already authorized.
Search and retrieval have explicit MCP output schemas. Structured and text tool results contain the same data; all metadata results identify dataset_id. The retrieve manifest is a bounded summary, not the full evidence. Up to 20 series_summaries identify series[index] and give counts, bounds and units; truncation flags disclose omissions. Non-null bounds exclude explicit null rows; missing_value_count does not count absent periods. Three previews sample across up to three series. The agent must have access to the MCP server's artifact_path; there are no post-retrieval MCP tools.
Reuse previewed codes before browsing more. Codelist searches tolerate case, spacing and punctuation; returned source codes remain unchanged and must be passed verbatim to retrieval. Similar matches remain separate choices; codelists do not establish available observation combinations.

ABS metadata exposes key_order, dimensions and codelists directly. ABS concepts are limited to those referenced by the selected data structure, including measures and roles; unreferenced_concept_count discloses omitted scheme members. Complete codelists and used definitions remain available. ABS, RBA and DCCEEW metadata preview up to 10 codes per codelist; OECD/Pacific resolve structures and complete codelists by agency, ID and version, reject ambiguous structures and incomplete authoritative code lists, preview complete embedded lists and resolve dimension labels without additional downloads; follow next_offset using get_metadata with dimension, codeSearch and codeOffset. These browsing parameters also apply to Pacific, OECD and Comtrade codelists and World Bank/IMF AREA codes. Comtrade code lists are fetched live; browse REPORTER, PARTNER, HS, FLOW, FREQUENCY, SECOND_PARTNER, CUSTOMS and TRANSPORT. OECD supports dimension selections and preserves separate series by the full SDMX dimension key. For Pacific data, search with provider PDH and use retrieve.sourceFilters to select source codes. Preserve unit multipliers, observation status and publication annotations from the saved JSON. Every source feeds one normalized live catalogue and FTS index, cached per session for 24 hours. Search reports stale/unavailable sources; dataset metadata remains a separate step.
The calling agent chooses calculations, charts, files and response format. No web app or model API key is needed.

The agent controls scope: ABS/OECD/Pacific accept named sourceFilters or a positional dataKey. ABS/Pacific/RBA/DCCEEW allow all-series retrieval. RBA accepts multiple Series IDs joined by +; DCCEEW accepts a discovered sheet, group or all supported data sheets. All five support source-format period bounds. World Bank/IMF accept area codes and year bounds. Search/metadata are discovery aids, not mandatory call gates. Missing selections produce coverage_gaps while preserving available evidence; malformed or ignored filters, unverifiable/truncated responses and wholly empty results fail explicitly. Macro source_row fields retain raw publisher observations; point.unit preserves unit changes. Comtrade supports HS 2/4/6-digit codes, annual/monthly years and optional secondary-partner, customs and transport filters; defaults are totals. Its public preview limit remains a source constraint. See AGENTS.md for development checks.

Local startup checks configuration, SQLite FTS5 and session-directory write access before the stdio server accepts requests. Provider availability is reported through catalogue source status.

Tool failures set isError and return equivalent structured/text error objects: code, message, retryable, retry_after_seconds, failed request (or request_truncated), and provider host/status when known. Inspect isError before applying the success output schema. Source GETs use at most two concurrent requests per host/process and one transient retry with at most five seconds of added waiting; longer cooldowns are returned to the agent. Retry-After dates and seconds are honored. Retry requests preserve source and parameters.

Catalogue queries preserve Unicode letters and numbers and normalize equivalent Unicode spellings; matching uses the shared SQLite FTS index. Search supports explicit match=any|all|phrase through the same index: any matches term prefixes, all requires every searchable term, and phrase preserves adjacent word order and filler words. Narrow searches never silently broaden; retain the matching mode when paging.
